questions.question: The railway system connecting St-Petersburg to Vladivostok is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trans – Siberian Railways**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Trans–Siberian Railway:

 
 
• This is a trans–Siberian Railways major rail route of Russia that runs from St. Petersburg in the west to Vladivostok on the Pacific Coast in the **east passing through Moscow, Ufa, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk, Chita and Khabarovsk.**
 
• It is the most important route in Asia and the longest (9,332 km) double-tracked and electrified transcontinental railway in the world.
 
• It has helped in opening up its Asian region to West European markets.
 
• It runs across the Ural Mountains Ob and Yenisei rivers Chita is an important agro centre and Irkutsk is a fur centre.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://d33wubrfki0l68.cloudfront.net/8d70b5e608a207057e52c2294ff0a28e369d6650/b0bd7/assets/images/russia-st-petersburg-1.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Trans Arabian Railway__

 __
 
• This is a concept as yet that has been approved by Saudi Arabia.
 
• This rail route will connect Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar.
 
• This ambitious project is called the GCC Rail network.
 
• Russian Railways is interested in constructing this project. 
 
 
 
• Trans European Railway__
 __
 
• It is a project by United Nations Economic Commission for Europe 
 
• It is a joint project with Tran European Motorways. 
 
• It aims at connecting Central, East, and South-Eastern Countries. 
 
 
 
• Trans-Asian Railway__
 
 
• It is a plan to construct a freight train network across Asia to Europe.
 
• The project is under the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP).

questions.question: The Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in Lok Sabha on August 8, 2022. The Bill amends the Electricity Act established in _______.

• The Electricity Act 2003:

questions.question: Distance covered by object is ______ to time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**directly proportional**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We know that Distance Travelled by an **Object = Speed x Time**.
 
• In order to replace the sign of equality with **proportionally**, either time or speed must be constant.
 
• As distance travelled is directly proportional to time.
 
• Therefore the speed of the object must be constant.
 
• This type of motion is also called **Uniform Motion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **motion **of an object can be uniform or non-uniform based on its velocity.
 
• The **velocity **of an object is the displacement per unit of time.
 
• Velocity is defined as a vector measurement of the rate and direction of motion of an object.
 
• Velocity formula when an object moving in a straight line: **r=d/t**.
 
 
• *"**r**" is the rate or speed, "**d**" is the distance moved, and "**t**" is the time it takes to complete the movement.*
 
 
 
• The **acceleration **of a moving object is the rate of change in velocity.

questions.question: “All India Muslim League” was established in 1906 at ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• All India Muslim League was established On 30 December 1906, a conference took place under the control of Nawab Salim Ulla Khan of Dhaka.
 
• The constitution of this league was made in 1907 in Karachi Pakistan.
 
• Its first session was held in 1907 in Karachi.
 
• The first session of the All India Muslim League was presided over by Aga Kha.
 
• Muslim League supported the partition of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The partition of Bengal in 1905 was introduced by Lord Curzon.
 
• He issued the order of partition of Bengal in July 1905 and the partition took effect in October 1905.
 
• The Eastern part of Bengal has the majority of the Muslim population and the western part of Bengal has the majority of the Hindu population while the central region is comprised of both religions.
 
• The partition of Bengal was made in order to carry out effective administration and discourage Hindu and Muslim unity.
 
• River Bhagirathi served as a physical partitioner between East Bengal and West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Vote**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The right to vote in India is guaranteed by the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1951, subject to certain limitations.
 
• Every citizen over the age of 18 has the right to vote under Article 326 of the Constitution.
 
• The Right to vote in India is a Constitutional Right and not a Fundamental Right.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are six fundamental rights recognized by the Indian constitution:

 
 
• Right to equality (Articles. 14-18)
 
• Right to freedom (Articles. 19-22) The right to freedom includes freedom of speech and expression
 
• Right against exploitation (Articles. 23-24)
 
• Right to freedom of religion (Articles. 25-28)
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles. 29-30), and
 
• Right to constitutional remedies (Articles. 32-35)

questions.question: Who among the following was the guru of Pandit Ravi Shankar?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Allauddin Khan totally reshaped Indian classical music's Maihar Gharana. **
 
• He was also known as Baba Allauddin Khan.
 
• He was born in Shibpur village in Brahmanbaria (in present-day Bangladesh) in 1862.
 
• He was an Indian sarod player.
 
• He was the guru of Pandit Ravi Shankar.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/45602890c77603b767ebe848bbca3cef939315d0bd51048cdae75a9bd42c1978.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ravi Shankar was a Sitar Player and composer.
 
• A sitar virtuoso, he became the world's best-known exponent of North Indian classical music in the second half of the 20th century and influenced many musicians in India and throughout the world.
 
• He was born on 7 April 1920 in Varanasi and died on 11 December 2012 in La Jolla, California, United States. 
 
• He was awarded Bharat Ratna, Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award, and more.
 
• He is an Indian musician, player of the sitar, composer, and founder of the National Orchestra of India.
 
• Sitar, a stringed instrument of the lute family that is popular in northern India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Vitamin A:

 
 
• It is fat soluble.
 
• Its scientific name is **R****etinol**.
 
• Its deficiency causes xeropthalmia.
 
• Milk, butter and liver are a source of vitamin A.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin B12:**
 
 
• Vitamin B12 is also known as cobalamin.
 
• It is a water-soluble vitamin involved in the metabolism of every cell of the human body.
 
• It is one of eight B vitamins.
 
• All forms of vitamin B12 contain the biochemically rare element cobalt (Co) positioned in the centre of a corrin ring.
 
 
 
• Vitamin C:
 
 
• It is a water-soluble vitamin.
 
• It is also known as Ascorbic acid.
 
• Scurvy is caused by not having enough vitamin C in our diet
 
• Vitamin C is mainly found in fruit and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin D:**
 
 
• **Vitamin D** is a group of fat-soluble secosteroids responsible for increasing intestinal absorption of calcium, magnesium, and phosphate, and multiple other biological effects.
 
• In humans, the most important compounds in this group are vitamin **D3 (also known as cholecalciferol) and vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol).**
 
• Cholecalciferol and ergocalciferol can be ingested from the diet and from supplements.
 
• Only a few foods contain vitamin D.
 
• The major natural source of the vitamin is the synthesis of cholecalciferol in the skin from cholesterol through a chemical reaction that is dependent on sun exposure (specifically UVB radiation).

questions.question: The first complete census taken in India is in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The first complete Census was taken in India in __1881.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **census **is an official enumeration of population done periodically. In India, the first census was held in the year **1872.**
 
• **The first complete census, however, was taken in the year 1881.** Since then, censuses have been held regularly every tenth year.
 
• The Indian Census is the most comprehensive source of demographic, social and economic data about India.

• It is Asia’s largest bird atlas in terms of geographical extent, sampling efforts, and species coverage derived from the aggregation of 25,000 checklists.
 
• It has details of 94 very rare species, 103 rare species, 110 common species, etc.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about inertia.

options.text: Greater the mass, greater the inertia
Lesser the weight, greater the inertia
Lesser the mass, greater the inertia
Greater the mass, lesser the inertia

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greater the mass, greater the inertia**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Inertia: 

 
• An inherent property of all the bodies by virtue of which they cannot change their state of rest or uniform motion along a straight line by their own is called inertia.
 
• The natural tendency of an object to resist the change in its state of rest or of state of uniform motion is called Inertia.
 
• Inertia is the measure of the mass of a body.
 
• Inertia is not a physical quantity, it is only a property of the body which depends on the mass of the body.
 
• Inertia has no units and no dimensions.
 
• From the above, it is clear that the property of the body which depends on the mass of the body i.e., the mass of an object is a measure of its inertia.
 
• **Greater is the mass of the body, more is the inertia of that body. **

questions.question: The Anantraj Sagar Tank was built by the ______ rulers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__**Vijayanagara**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Vijaynagar Kingdom (1336-1546 A.D.) in the south took keen interest in building large and small storage tanks.
 
• Anantraj Sagar tank was built with a **1.37 km** long earthen dam across the Maldevi river.
 
• The well-known Korangal dam was built under King **Krishnadevraya.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Vijayanagara empire__:

 
 
• They ruled with their capital Hampi.
 
• They played a major role in protecting the Hindu religion and culture in south India.
 
• Harihara and Bukka were the founders of this dynasty.
 
• Dewankhana is a 40-pillared hall to the right side of the emperor’s palace.
 
• Boundaries of the land were demarcated by stones called Vamanamudreyakallu or Lingamudreyakallu.
 
• They issued gold silver and copper coins. Gold coins were called Gadyana, Varaha or Honnu, Prathapa, Hana, Visa, and Kasu based on their denominations.
 
• Mangalore, Bhatkala, Barkur, and Honnavara are the major port cities during the Vijayanagara times.
 
• The Boar / Varaha (an avatar of Vishnu) is the royal emblem of Vijayanagara rulers
 
• They issued nearly 7000 inscriptions, half of them are in the Kannada language and the rest are in Tamil, Telugu, and Sanskrit.
 
• Ramabhyudhayam was written by Rajanatha Dindima in the Sanskrit language. 
 
• Kumara Ramana Kathe was written by Poet Nanjunda in the Kannada Language. 
 
• Achuthabhyudhayam was written by Dindima II in Sanskrit.
 
• Varadambika Parinayam was written by Tirumalamba.
 
• Untouchability was still in practice in the kingdom.
 
• The secretaries in the kingdom were called Rayasa.
 
• Karyakarta is a man who looked after the emperor’s personal works.
 
• Land revenue was the chief source of Income, and was assessed after deciding the gross product of the land.
